evidence.claim: Step-up authentication passed: the cardholder completed the one-time passcode challenge and confirmed the $100.07 online purchase of 2016-12-07 was made by them on their own iOS device, noting they routinely use several devices.
The flagged amount is below the card's norm: $100.07 against a 180d mean of $177.52 (amount_z -0.34, 0.56x mean, card max $1,104.08), so no value anomaly.

Transaction is in the card's home region 330 (85 of 90 baseline txns) and home country 87 (90 of 90); new_region_for_card is false and the card was already used in region 330 on 2016-12-02, 12-03 and 12-07.
Episode window contains exactly one online transaction; no card-testing run (<$5 authorizations), no just-under-$500 run, no 2-4 transaction burst - so pattern 2/3 lacks its defining burst.
The card has 19 distinct devices in 180 days with no dominant device (top device used only twice), so a New device flag is weakly informative for this account; no proxy was recorded.

The only rare shared device ('Windows | Windows 7 | chrome 64.0 | 1600x900', 53 cards all-time, 2 in window, linked to C00854-K2) does not appear on the flagged transaction, which used 'iOS Device | iOS 9.3.5 | mobile safari 9.0 | 1024x768'; the link is therefore not evidence about this transaction.
Region 330 newcomer fraud rate is 0.13 versus a 0.10 base rate across 275 active cards - a negligible lift, and this card is not a newcomer to region 330.

Five structurally linked closed cases with higher model scores ($50.06 at 0.85, $200.06 at 0.90, $150.01 at 0.94, $99.93 at 0.85, $49.95 at 0.84) were all cleared after the cardholder confirmed a new phone or travel.
Semantic memory returns five near-identical narratives (CC-3520, CC-0010, CC-0871, CC-5462, CC-0831, similarity 0.78-0.79), all cleared as legitimate purchases from a new phone.

Prior confirmed account-takeover cases on this same card (CC-2400 $350.99, CC-2717 $896.08, CC-2857 $539.97) all date from 18-30 August 2016 and involved 2-6 mixed-channel transactions; the December alert is a single same-region online charge and does not match that signature.
Policy R3 directs CLOSE_NO_FRAUD when the customer confirms the transaction; policy \u00a76 permits stopping once probability is at or below 0.15 with at least two independent pieces of evidence.

case.summary: Case HHG-005 was opened on a model score alone (0.54) for a $100.07 online transaction 3523199 on card C02923-K1. The only genuine anomaly was that the iOS device was New for the account, but the card has used 19 devices in 180 days, the amount is below its mean, and the transaction sits in the card's home region 330 and home country 87 with no burst, no tiny-authorization run and no proxy. A step-up authentication challenge was issued under policy R1; the cardholder passed the one-time passcode and confirmed the purchase, stating they routinely use several devices. This matches a large body of closed cases (CC-0219, CC-0189, CC-3520 and others) cleared on identical facts, and it does not resemble this customer's August 2016 account-takeover episodes (CC-2400, CC-2717, CC-2857), which were multi-transaction and mixed-channel. The rare-device link to C00854-K2 involves a Windows profile that does not appear on this transaction and should not drive action here. Recommend CLOSE_NO_FRAUD under R3 and add the iOS device profile to the account.
